text:
Elena: Flagging a few issues in the function-calling + structured-output guide after user feedback. main concerns: outdated JS snippet, missing python example, and a confusing schema that allows extra fields.
Ravi: which page exactly? link?
Elena: /docs/guides/function-calling/structured-output.md — top JS snippet uses `callTool()` and the schema includes `additionalProperties: true` which we don't want as canonical.
Morgan: I can swap to v1 API and add a concise Python example. We should show one canonical strict JSON schema and then a 1-line lenient note.
Chris: Good call. Also noticed the code fence titles break our markdown renderer if we include language+title. Keep standard fences.
Ravi: proposed JS snippet (v1):
```js
// v1: invokeTool client usage
const resp = await client.invokeTool('extract_entities', {
  input: articleText,
  params: { temperature: 0 }
});
console.log(resp.output);
```
Morgan: Python snippet to add: 
```py
# v1 python client
resp = client.invoke_tool('extract_entities', input=article_text, params={'temperature':0})
print(resp.output)
```
Elena: nice. For schema we should recommend strict mode: `additionalProperties: false` and required fields. Example to paste: 
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "entities": { "type": "array", "items": { "type": "string" } },
    "count": { "type": "integer" }
  },
  "required": ["entities"],
  "additionalProperties": false
}
```
Ravi: add a short prose note: "If you need backward compatibility, include a migration example mapping `response_schema` -> `outputSchema` and show how to tolerate an extra `metadata` field in parsing." Keep it small.
Morgan: I'll add a tiny tolerant variation showing `additionalProperties: true` with a short comment.
Chris: Also add an example of programmatic validation + graceful fallback in both JS and Python. People copy-paste blindly so show them the safe path.
Ravi: validation examples:
```js
try {
  const parsed = JSON.parse(resp.output);
  validate(parsed, schema); // throws if invalid
} catch (err) {
  // log + fallback
}
```
```py
try:
  parsed = json.loads(resp.output)
  validate(parsed, schema)
except Exception as e:
  # fallback: return safe default or re-call with stricter system prompt
```
Elena: one more: our caching guide mention should be linked. small warning: deterministic tool outputs + prefix caching can return stale results in long-lived sessions. Link to caching guide: https://docs.redwood.ai/guides/caching#prefix-kv
Chris: I'll fix two broken anchors I found in the guide and remove a leftover reference to /integrations/old-tooling.
Morgan: I opened branch `docs/structured-output-v1` with JS/Python snippets and schema updates. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/507
Ravi: opened `docs/migrate-response-schema` with migration note and a tiny unit test for the fixture. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/508
Docs Bot: Running jobs: docs/link-check on PR #507 and docs/schema-lint on #508.
PreviewBot: Previews queued: https://preview.docs.redwood.ai/pr-507-508/ (48h)
Elena: CI for #508 failed schema-lint complaining about a trailing comma in the fixtures JSON. small fix pushed.
Morgan: updated the markdown to remove fenced code titles and fixed the header anchors. pushed.
Ravi: tests pass locally for migration fixture. pushing now.
Chris: quick review plan: 1) confirm snippets in both languages 2) schema is copy/paste ready 3) migration blurb present 4) caching note + link 5) TOC anchors fixed.
Elena: can we also add a brief note about typed-language mapping (e.g., TypeScript interfaces or Go structs) to show how `additionalProperties: false` helps? one sentence.
Morgan: good idea, I'll add a tiny TypeScript interface example.
Ravi: LGTM from my side, will approve once previews are up.
Morgan: previews green. Requesting final review.
Chris: gave an approve.
Elena: merged both PRs. Please add a changelog bullet under "Docs" for this release noting the v1 snippets + migration tip.
Ravi: added changelog entry.
Elena: thanks all — closing thread. :white_check_mark:
